title: Pharmacy Override Activity — Opioid and Antibiotic Order Duplication

fields.organization: Ottawa River Regional Medical Center — Pharmacy
fields.location: Emergency Department and Post-Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU)
fields.summary: During the 18:30–19:00 shift, opioid medication pulls from override cabinets in the ED and PACU increased by 200% compared to baseline. A review of paper order sheets revealed three duplicate antibiotic orders for the same open-fracture trauma patient. The covering resident re-wrote orders twice due to EHR unavailability. No pharmacist was assigned to the ED or PACU during the surge. The override log shows 47 pulls since 17:00, with no verification of dispensing against the paper order sheet.

findings.item: Override cabinet access logged per shift
findings.notes: No log entry for 18:45–19:00; last entry at 18:30

findings.item: Pharmacist presence in ED and PACU
findings.notes: No pharmacist assigned to either area during peak surge hours

findings.item: Duplicate medication orders on paper
findings.notes: Three identical antibiotic orders for patient T-11, documented on separate sheets

findings.item: High-alert drug verification by two staff
findings.notes: No second-person verification for opioid or antibiotic orders

findings.item: Paper order sheet retention and tracking
findings.notes: Order sheets scattered across workstations; no central tracking

findings.item: Medication dispensing against order sheet
findings.notes: One dispensing error found: ampicillin 500mg IV not verified against order

findings.item: Override mode activation status
findings.notes: Override mode active on all cabinets; no unauthorized access detected

findings.item: Barcode scanning for high-alert drugs
findings.notes: System down; not applicable

findings.item: EHR read-only access for order review
findings.notes: EHR available for read-only access only; no edits permitted

findings.item: Verbal order read-back and sign-off
findings.notes: No read-back record for 12 verbal orders in the last 90 minutes

actionsTaken: Assigned pharmacist to ED and PACU at 19:05
Initiated 30-minute override pull count for all ED and PACU units
Cancelled duplicate antibiotic orders for T-11 with physician and pharmacist approval
Instructed resident to use only one paper order sheet per patient, to be retained in the ED log
recommendations: Maintain pharmacist presence in ED and PACU during all mass casualty incidents
Implement mandatory 30-minute override pull counts during downtime
Require dual verification for all high-alert drugs, including opioids and antibiotics, during downtime
Reinforce verbal order protocol: read-back and signature within 24 hours, with documentation in the downtime log
fields.photosNote: 5 photos attached: IMG_0413-0417 (paper order sheets, override log, pharmacist in ED, duplicate antibiotic order, tracking board)

instructorNote: This inject tests the team's ability to enforce downtime procedures under surge conditions. Watch for the CNO to assign pharmacists and implement verification protocols. The duplicate order is a direct result of the EHR being read-only and no centralized order tracking.
